newsitem.title: USA: USWC Alaskan crudes slump after steep discount.
newsitem.headline: USWC Alaskan crudes slump after steep discount.

text.p: U.S. West Coast Alaskan crude prices slumped late Friday, after an oil company sold a cargo at a sharp discount, buyers said.
West Coast spot traders said Exxon sold a 400,000 barrel cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at $1.32 off West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
The discount, 0.27 cents a barrel lower than the last deal, offset a slight gain in West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the price ANS is calculated off.
Outright prices stood $18.08/18.28 a barrel, down 32 cents from yesterday's levels.
Texaco finished unloading a 400,000 barrel cargo of South Blend into its refinery at Anacortes, Washington, Thursday and expects another to be delivered May 20, traders said.
Shell will receive a 420,000 barrel cargo of Cano Limon crude in mid to late May.
A 2,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) shipment for California heavy grade in May sold at postings early this week, traders said.
